WHY IT MATTERS. Hybrid rice raised yields substantially across China and beyond and was developed publicly, with the breeder's name attached rather than a patent portfolio. The company now carrying that name operating commercially in GM traits is the whole trajectory of this industry compressed into one brand.

name: Bioceres / Moolec — molecular farming
desc: WHAT. A company engineering food crops to produce animal proteins inside the plant — pork protein in soy, bovine protein in peas. WHERE IT SITS. Molecular farming, where the crop is a factory and the product is not a plant protein at all. WHY IT MATTERS. A soy plant containing pig protein is not covered by any labelling scheme designed around allergens, dietary restriction or religious observance. Whether that matters is a question for the people whose diets depend on those categories, and none of them have been asked.

name: ISAAA AfriCenter
desc: WHAT. The African office of the biotechnology information service, producing country briefs, training journalists and running public communication on crop biotechnology. WHERE IT SITS. The information layer in countries where approval decisions are pending, funded largely by the industry it reports on. WHY IT MATTERS. Its country briefs are the most-cited summaries of African biotechnology status, including by people opposing it, because little else covers the same ground. Listed at low trust: useful, comprehensive, and produced by an interested party, which is the ordinary condition of information in this field.

name: Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service
desc: WHAT. Kenya's plant health authority, running seed certification, variety registration and the testing that detects GM material in imports. WHERE IT SITS. The enforcement layer beneath the biosafety decisions — where a rule either is or is not testable. WHY IT MATTERS. Kenya has the laboratory capacity to test, which most importing countries on this map do not. That capacity is what turns a labelling or import rule from a statement into an enforceable one, and it is the single most useful thing a country in this position can invest in.

name: CIMMYT — maize and wheat genebank
desc: WHAT. The CGIAR centre holding the world's largest maize and wheat collections, in maize's centre of origin, distributing germplasm to breeders worldwide. WHERE IT SITS. The genetic reservoir nearly every commercial maize and wheat variety on Earth traces back to. WHY IT MATTERS. Its material moves under a standard agreement that keeps it available and unpatentable in the form supplied. That arrangement is the main thing standing between the world's staple crop diversity and the enclosure the rest of this map documents, and it depends on continued funding rather than on any law.

name: MASIPAG
desc: WHAT. A Philippine farmer-scientist network that breeds and distributes rice varieties selected by farmers themselves, and which brought the litigation that revoked the Golden Rice and Bt eggplant permits. WHERE IT SITS. The clearest working example anywhere of farmer-led breeding operating as an alternative rather than an objection. WHY IT MATTERS. It does both halves: it maintains hundreds of farmer-selected rice varieties in circulation, and it won in court on procedure. An opposition that also produces seed is a different proposition from one that only files comments.

name: American Seed Trade Association
desc: WHAT. The US seed industry's trade association, active on plant variety protection, seed treatment rules and the regulatory treatment of gene editing. WHERE IT SITS. The domestic counterpart to CropLife, working seed law rather than pesticide law. WHY IT MATTERS. It maintains the voluntary transparency database that gene-edited varieties are listed in where no notification is required. **The public record of what is being planted is kept by the sector planting it**, which is a fact about the regulation rather than about the companies.

name: Seed Savers Exchange
desc: WHAT. A US non-profit maintaining and distributing thousands of heirloom and open-pollinated varieties through a member seed exchange and its own collection. WHERE IT SITS. The living counterweight to the genebank: varieties kept in circulation rather than in cold storage. WHY IT MATTERS. A variety in a freezer survives; a variety being grown adapts. The distinction matters because the material this map documents being enclosed is only useful to anyone if someone is still planting it.

name: Organic Seed Alliance
desc: WHAT. An organisation breeding and advocating for organic seed, publishing the periodic State of Organic Seed assessment of supply and demand. WHERE IT SITS. The supply constraint under organic certification — organic growers need organic seed, and there is not enough of it. WHY IT MATTERS. Its own surveys find most organic growers using conventional untreated seed under allowed exemptions, because organic seed is unavailable in the varieties they need. **Seed supply is a quieter lever on the organic sector than any biosafety rule**, and it is being pulled by market structure rather than by policy.

name: Scribe Therapeutics
desc: WHAT. A company engineering CRISPR proteins from scratch rather than adapting bacterial ones, aiming at improved specificity and delivery. WHERE IT SITS. Editors as designed molecules rather than borrowed ones. WHY IT MATTERS. A protein designed rather than discovered is not covered by patents on naturally occurring systems, which is part of the point. The patent fight this map documents is being routed around by building tools that were never anyone's to claim.

name: Tome Biosciences / large-payload integration
desc: WHAT. Companies developing programmable integration of whole genes rather than edits to existing sequence, using engineered recombinases. WHERE IT SITS. The step past editing: inserting a complete functional gene at a chosen site. WHY IT MATTERS. Regulatory carve-outs for gene editing rest on nothing foreign being added. Programmable integration adds a whole gene, so it lands back inside the transgenic definition — which is the first technique in years to move in that direction rather than out of it.

name: iGEM Foundation
desc: WHAT. The international student synthetic biology competition, with hundreds of teams a year building engineered organisms and depositing standardised parts. WHERE IT SITS. Where the next generation of this industry is trained, and where its parts registry lives. WHY IT MATTERS. It runs its own biosafety and security review for student projects, which is more scrutiny than several national frameworks apply to commercial work. The competition also normalises building organisms as an ordinary undergraduate exercise, and both of those are true at once.

name: Cyagen / knockout mouse repositories — IMPC
desc: WHAT. The International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium, systematically knocking out every protein-coding gene in the mouse and publishing the resulting phenotypes. WHERE IT SITS. The most systematic programme of vertebrate engineering ever undertaken, publicly funded across several countries. WHY IT MATTERS. The stated goal is a knockout line for all ~20,000 mouse genes. That is a complete catalogue of what breaking each gene does to a mammal, and it is being assembled openly, which makes it both the best documentation in this facet and its largest single undertaking.

name: Physicians Committee / animal testing policy
desc: WHAT. A medical advocacy organisation campaigning to replace animal testing with non-animal methods, active on the US legislation that removed the animal-testing requirement for drug approval. WHERE IT SITS. The organised pressure against the laboratory animal facet, from inside medicine. WHY IT MATTERS. The FDA Modernization Act removed the statutory requirement that drugs be tested in animals before human trials. **The requirement is gone and the practice largely continues**, because regulators still expect the data and sponsors still supply it. A law changing and nothing changing is worth documenting precisely.

name: Cargill
desc: WHAT. One of the largest privately held companies in the world, trading grain, crushing oilseed, producing animal feed and processing meat across every continent. WHERE IT SITS. The middle of the commodity chain — between the farm and everything downstream. WHY IT MATTERS. It is private, so it publishes far less than any listed company on this map, and it handles a very large share of the world's traded grain. **The single largest mover of engineered crop output discloses the least about it**, and no rule requires otherwise.

name: Archer Daniels Midland
desc: WHAT. A major grain processor and ingredient producer, including fermentation-derived ingredients and animal feed. WHERE IT SITS. Alongside Cargill in the handling layer, but listed, so its filings are public. WHY IT MATTERS. Reading ADM's disclosures alongside Cargill's silence shows how much of this industry's visibility is an accident of corporate form rather than of policy. The same activity is documented or not depending on whether shares are traded.

name: Nucleus Genomics
desc: WHAT. A company selling consumer genomic analysis including polygenic scoring, and marketing embryo screening on traits beyond disease risk. WHERE IT SITS. The furthest commercial edge of embryo selection, sold directly. WHY IT MATTERS. Professional genetics bodies have stated that polygenic embryo screening is not supported for clinical use. It is sold anyway, because embryo selection faces none of the approval requirements a drug or device would. **The gap between what the science supports and what may lawfully be sold is the whole of this**, and it is widening rather than closing.

name: Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology — clinic outcome reports
desc: WHAT. The searchable clinic-by-clinic outcome data underlying US national ART reporting, showing cycles, transfers and live births per clinic. WHERE IT SITS. The one place a prospective patient can compare clinics on outcomes. WHY IT MATTERS. Success rates depend heavily on which patients a clinic accepts, so a clinic can raise its published figures by declining harder cases. The data is real and the comparison it invites is not straightforward, which is worth saying wherever it is cited.

name: Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research
desc: WHAT. A US non-profit created by Congress in the 2014 Farm Bill to fund agricultural research, required to match every federal dollar with private money. WHERE IT SITS. Public research funding structurally bound to private co-funding. WHY IT MATTERS. The matching requirement means no project is funded unless a private partner also wants it. That is a design choice written into statute, and it decides which agricultural questions can be asked with public money at all.

name: Nuffield Council on Bioethics
desc: WHAT. An independent body that examines ethical questions in biology and medicine, whose reports on genome editing in human reproduction and in farmed animals are widely cited. WHERE IT SITS. Deliberative work with no statutory power, in a country whose regulators do have it. WHY IT MATTERS. Its 2018 report concluded heritable genome editing could be ethically acceptable in some circumstances, which surprised people expecting a prohibition. Citing it honestly means citing that conclusion, and the map is more useful for including a considered position it does not simply endorse.

name: UK Biobank
desc: WHAT. A cohort of half a million volunteers with genomic, imaging and health-record data, accessible to approved researchers worldwide including commercial ones. WHERE IT SITS. The model most national genomic programmes have copied. WHY IT MATTERS. Access is by approved application rather than by purchase, and the resulting analyses must be returned to the resource. That is a materially different arrangement from a company owning the dataset outright, and it is the clearest available answer to what the alternative to enclosure looks like in human genomics.

name: Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global — ethics exclusions
desc: WHAT. The world's largest sovereign wealth fund, which publishes the companies it has excluded on ethical grounds and the reasoning for each. WHERE IT SITS. The one large investor that states publicly why it will not hold something. WHY IT MATTERS. Exclusion decisions are published with their reasoning, which makes them citable and comparable in a way no other institutional investor's are. For anyone pursuing the shareholder route this map keeps pointing at, it is the worked example of what a documented divestment argument looks like.

name: Swiss GMO moratorium — Federal Office for the Environment
desc: WHAT. Switzerland's environment office, administering a moratorium on the commercial cultivation of GM crops that parliament has extended repeatedly since 2005. WHERE IT SITS. Twenty years of a temporary measure, renewed each time it approached expiry. WHY IT MATTERS. A moratorium extended five times is a permanent policy that never had to be argued as one. Whether that is democratic caution or avoidance depends on the reader, and the map is better for stating the mechanism rather than the verdict.

name: Global 2000 / Friends of the Earth Austria
desc: WHAT. The Austrian environmental organisation that commissions independent testing of food and feed for GM content and publishes the results. WHERE IT SITS. Independent testing capacity outside both government and industry. WHY IT MATTERS. Almost nobody outside a regulator or a company runs their own detection. Where an organisation does, its results are the only figures in the argument that neither side commissioned — which is why they get cited by both.

name: Wageningen University & Research
desc: WHAT. The world's leading agricultural university, running crop genetics, editing and food systems research, with substantial industry partnership funding. WHERE IT SITS. Where a very large share of the field's researchers are trained and much of its published evidence is produced. WHY IT MATTERS. Its funding mix of public money and industry partnership is disclosed and is also the ordinary condition of agricultural science. The evidence base this whole argument runs on is produced substantially inside that arrangement, which is worth knowing whichever conclusion you reach from it.

name: Anastasia / RNAi biopesticide sector
desc: WHAT. The EPA registration route for sprayed double-stranded RNA products, which silence a gene in a target pest without modifying any organism. WHERE IT SITS. A category that is neither an engineered organism nor a conventional chemical. WHY IT MATTERS. Nothing living is altered, so no biosafety framework applies; the mechanism is sequence-specific, so pesticide assumptions about dose and residue do not fit either. **Both regulatory categories were built for something else, and the product is sold while the question of which one governs it stays open.**

name: Verily / Debug — automated rearing systems
desc: WHAT. Automated mass-rearing, sex-sorting and release systems for sterile mosquitoes, built by a technology company rather than an entomology institute. WHERE IT SITS. Where release capacity stopped being limited by biology and started being limited by engineering. WHY IT MATTERS. When releasing tens of millions of insects is a logistics problem, the only remaining constraint is permission — and the permission systems were designed when rearing capacity was the practical brake.

name: Ceres Nanosciences / environmental RNA monitoring
desc: WHAT. Technologies for concentrating and detecting genetic material from environmental samples — water, soil, wastewater. WHERE IT SITS. The detection side, which barely exists compared to the release side. WHY IT MATTERS. Environmental DNA methods could find engineered sequences in a river or a field margin without knowing in advance what to look for. The capability is developing for pathogen surveillance; nobody is funding it to watch releases.

name: Wisconsin Cryobank / amphibian biobanking
desc: WHAT. Coordinated cryopreservation of amphibian sperm and cell lines, alongside captive assurance colonies for species collapsing from chytrid fungus. WHERE IT SITS. The taxon losing species fastest, and the one where biobanking is furthest behind. WHY IT MATTERS. Amphibians are dying out faster than they are being sampled. Whatever is banked now is the entire set of options anyone will have later, and the sampling is being done by a handful of underfunded programmes.

name: Rewilding and genetic rescue — Florida panther precedent
desc: WHAT. The introduction of Texas cougars into the remnant Florida panther population in 1995, which reversed inbreeding effects and tripled the population. WHERE IT SITS. Genetic rescue done by moving animals rather than editing them, and the case every engineered proposal is measured against. WHY IT MATTERS. It worked, it is decades old, and it required no biotechnology. Any engineered genetic rescue has to explain what it adds over translocation, and that comparison is rarely made explicit in the proposals.

name: Medpace
desc: WHAT. A clinical research organisation running trials across therapeutic areas, listed and therefore disclosing more than its private-equity peers. WHERE IT SITS. The mid-tier of the trial industry, and one of the few remaining listed pure-play CROs. WHY IT MATTERS. Its filings state trial volumes, backlog and therapeutic mix. That is the clearest public view of how the contract layer actually earns, and it exists only because the company happens to be listed.

name: Emulate / organ-on-chip
desc: WHAT. Microfluidic devices lined with human cells that reproduce organ-level responses, used as an alternative to animal testing. WHERE IT SITS. The technology the FDA Modernization Act was written to permit. WHY IT MATTERS. The law now allows non-animal methods and regulators still expect animal data, so adoption depends on which sponsors are willing to go first. **The constraint stopped being legal and became conventional**, which is harder to change and gets far less attention.

name: Certara / in-silico trial simulation
desc: WHAT. Modelling and simulation used to predict drug behaviour and, increasingly, to replace some trial arms with simulated controls. WHERE IT SITS. Where evidence starts being generated by computation rather than by measurement. WHY IT MATTERS. A simulated control arm means fewer people receive placebo, which is a real gain. It also means part of the evidence for approval was produced by a model whose assumptions are commercial property, and regulators are accepting that.

name: Select Sires / bovine genetics cooperatives
desc: WHAT. A farmer-owned cooperative supplying dairy and beef semen, genomic testing and reproductive services across the United States and internationally. WHERE IT SITS. Cooperative ownership of cattle genetics, alongside the corporate suppliers. WHY IT MATTERS. Genomic selection has compressed dairy cattle generation intervals sharply, so a trait chosen now reaches a national herd within a few years. Whether the supplier is a cooperative or a corporation, the speed is the same — which suggests the pace is set by the technology and the market, not the ownership.

name: Sexing Technologies / STgenetics
desc: WHAT. The dominant supplier of sexed semen technology, allowing breeders to choose the sex of offspring at scale in cattle. WHERE IT SITS. Reproductive control upstream of genetics — deciding which animals are born at all. WHY IT MATTERS. Sexed semen means most dairy calves born are female, and the male calves that were the by-product are simply not conceived. It reduces a welfare problem by removing the animals from existence, which is a genuine improvement and worth naming precisely as what it is.

name: Royal Botanic Gardens Kew — Millennium Seed Bank
desc: WHAT. The world's largest wild plant seed bank, holding seed from tens of thousands of species with a focus on wild relatives and endangered flora. WHERE IT SITS. Wild plant diversity, as distinct from crop diversity — the material no agricultural genebank has a mandate to hold. WHY IT MATTERS. The wild relatives this map describes taking up engineered genes are the same material stored here. A bank of what a population used to be is the only reference against which a change can later be measured, and almost nowhere else is collecting it.

name: Legal & General / institutional stewardship
desc: WHAT. A large asset manager publishing its voting record and engagement priorities, including on agricultural and biodiversity risk. WHERE IT SITS. The stewardship end of institutional ownership — what a large holder does with its votes rather than whether it holds. WHY IT MATTERS. Voting records are published and searchable, so a claim that shareholders are indifferent can be checked rather than asserted. It is also where a resolution has to get support to pass, which makes the record the practical starting point for anyone attempting one.

name: Lonza — capacity allocation and Moderna
desc: WHAT. The company's disclosures on contract manufacturing capacity, including the arrangements that produced billions of vaccine doses. WHERE IT SITS. The single largest allocator of biologics manufacturing capacity outside the majors' own plants. WHY IT MATTERS. Which products get made, and when, is decided in commercial negotiations between a contractor and its clients. During a shortage that is a rationing decision, taken privately, by a company no health authority appoints or oversees.

name: VikingGenetics
desc: WHAT. A Nordic farmer-owned cattle breeding cooperative, running genomic selection across Danish, Swedish and Finnish herds. WHERE IT SITS. The European cooperative counterpart to the American bovine genetics suppliers. WHY IT MATTERS. It publishes breeding indexes that include health and longevity alongside yield, which most indexes historically did not. The composition of a breeding index decides what a national herd becomes, and it is set by a committee almost nobody outside the sector has heard of.

name: Testbiotech
desc: WHAT. A German institute producing independent scientific assessment of genetic engineering applications, and filing formal objections to EU authorisations. WHERE IT SITS. Almost the only body doing technical review of EFSA dossiers from outside industry or government. WHY IT MATTERS. Its submissions are the substantive scientific comments in EU authorisation files that did not come from an applicant. That a handful of staff constitute most of the independent technical scrutiny in the world's largest import market is a fact about the scrutiny, not about them.

name: Corporate Europe Observatory
desc: WHAT. A research and campaign organisation documenting lobbying in the EU institutions, including on the new genomic techniques file. WHERE IT SITS. The counterpart to the Transparency Register — reading the declarations and following what they connect to. WHY IT MATTERS. The register publishes numbers; someone has to read them against meeting records to make them mean anything. That work is done by a small number of organisations, and everyone arguing about EU biotechnology policy relies on it whether they cite it or not.
